items.text: Do not exceed this speed in any operation
Do not exceed this speed except in smooth air and then only with caution
VS0 — Stall speed in landing configuration (40° Flaps)
If enough runway remaining to land:
Fly runway heading to emergency landing site
Gain all the altitude you can! Pull back (gently) to use the aircraft’s momentum to gain altitude until airspeed falls off to the optimum glide speed (82 MPH IAS; 71 Knots).

items.response: OPTIMUM GLIDE SPEED 82 MPH IAS (71 KNOTS)

items.text: Trim the airplane for optimum glide speed

Find a suitable place to land and fly to it. If altitude and distance to selected site permit, try to set up a normal landing pattern. If that’s not possible, take what you can get. Make sure the approach results in a landing parallel to any furrows in the selected field.
If time permits, try to correct the problem:

items.response: BOTH MAGNETOS — START IF PROPELLER STOPPED
82 MPH IAS / 71 KNOTS (FLAPS UP); 76 MPH IAS / 66 KNOTS (FLAPS DOWN)
INSPECT — FLY OVER FIELD NOTING TERRAIN AND OBSTRUCTIONS, THEN RETRACT FLAPS ON REACHING SAFE ALTITUDE AND AIRSPEED.

items.text: Give location, situation and intentions. If already communicating with ATC, report situation to controller rather than using 121.5.

items.response: THROUGH DOOR — IF NECESSARY, OPEN WINDOW TO ALLOW CABIN TO FLOOD TO EQUALIZE PRESSURE SO DOOR CAN BE OPENED.

items.text: Crank engine with starter to suck fire into the engine
Continue running to try to suck fire into the engine
In either case if fire is not out in a few seconds
After using fire extinguisher within a closed cabin ventilate the cabin.

items.response: PERFORM SIDE-SLIP TO KEEP FLAMES AWAY FROM FUEL TANK AND CABIN

items.text: Fuel Level — Both Wings - Visual check
If needed get gas (AVGAS 100) before proceeding with other fuel tank related items.
Wing Tops — Inspect for loose screws, rivets and damage

items.response: ON - OBSERVE AMMETER DROP - THEN OFF

items.text: Walk around plane and visually check to see that all are operating.
Visually check from outside if not dark enough to see that it’s on from inside the cockpit.
Flap — Check freedom of movement and security.
Aileron — Check security and freedom of movement
Wing tip — Check for cracks; Check light security.
Fuel sump — Check sample for color, water and dirt.
Main landing gear — Check tire wear, brake pads, leaking brake fluid.
Nose gear — Check tire wear; Strut inflation; security
Engine compartment — Check for bird’s nests
Propeller — Check for nicks and security;
Air Filter — Check clean and security
Fuel sump — Check sample for color, water and dirt.
Main landing gear — Check tire wear, brake pads, leaking brake fluid.
Fuel sump — Check sample for color, water and dirt.
Pitot/Static — Check cover off; Check holes not obstructed.
Wing tip — Check for cracks; Check light security.
Aileron — Check security and freedom of movement.
Flap — Check freedom of movement and security.
Stall Warning Vane — Check for free operation
Check for loose rivets, screws and damage.
Stabilator — Check security and freedom of movement.
Rudder — Check security and freedom of movement.
Check for loose rivets, screws and damage
Brief passengers on use of belts/harnesses and requirements for wearing them.
Primer — Prime if required — Make sure locked in
Propeller Area — Call “Clear” & check prop area and behind plane
Radios — On and set to appropriate frequency. Call for radio check
Clearance — Check for things in way of wings — Check for people ahead of and behind plane
Flight Controls — Set for existing wind conditions
Brakes — Come to full stop immediately after starting taxi roll
Turn Coordinator — Should indicate turn in proper direction while taxiing.
Attitude Indicator — Very little change due to turns; Slight pitch indications due to acceleration or deceleration.
Altimeter — When set to current altimeter setting should indicate within 75 ft. of airport elevation.
VSI — Should indicate zero. If not, note indication and use for level indication in flight.
VORs — Check at local ground check point or against each other based on some receivable signal.
Set attitude indicator to level flight position. Set altimeter to runway altitude or locally reported altimeter setting. Set heading indicator to magnetic compass.
Comm Radio/VOR — Set to appropriate freqs
Parking brake — Set or hold foot brakes
RPM drop should not exceed 125 RPM on either magneto. RPM difference between magnetos should not exceed 50 RPM.

items.response: ON — CHECK FOR RPM DROP THEN BACK TO OFF

items.text: Oil pressure/Temperature; Suction; Ammeter - Create electrical load with landing light. Make sure no more than needle width deflection.
Fuel Pump — Momentarily Off; Check for good fuel pressure; On
Engine Instruments — Check while starting roll
RPM – In the green arc; Oil Pressure - In the green; Oil Temperature - In the green; Suction - In the green

items.response: LIFT NOSE WHEEL AT 60 MPH (52 KIAS)

items.text: Taxi — Maximum runway usage — Takeoff procedure should be started using ALL available runway. Taxi to end of runway and align with centerline.
Engine Instruments — Check before starting roll
RPM – In the green arc; Oil Pressure - In the green; Oil Temperature - In the green; Suction - In the green

items.response: 74 MPH (65 KIAS) UNTIL OBSTACLES CLEARED, THEN 85 MPH (74 KIAS)

items.text: Flaps — Retract at safe altitude with positive rate of climb.
Taxi — Keep rolling to avoid bogging down
If 25° flaps are used, with obstacles ahead, leave them extended until the obstacle is cleared and at a safe altitude.
Heading indicator — Calibrate against compass or runway heading
Engine Instruments — Check as starting roll
RPM – In the green arc; Oil Pressure - In the green; Oil Temperature - In the green; Suction - In the green
Allow the airplane to lift off as soon as possible (before reaching safe climb speed). Level off at a few feet above the ground and fly in ground effect until reaching normal climb speed.

items.response: 74 MPH (65 KIAS) UNTIL OBSTACLES CLEARED, THEN 85 MPH (74 KIAS)

items.text: Flaps — Retract at safe altitude with positive rate of climb.
Fuel Pump — Off at 1,000 AGL; Check fuel pressure
Airspeed — Let build to desired cruise speed
Throttle — Reduce to desired cruise setting

items.response: SEE POH CLIMB TABLE IN SECTION IV
RICH (FORWARD) BELOW 5,000 FT. LEANED FOR MAXIMUM RPM ABOVE 5,000.

items.text: Fuel Pump — On; Check fuel pressure
Power — Reduce to 1,300 to 1,500 RPM abeam approach end of runway
Airspeed — Let bleed off to less than 115 MPH (100 KIAS)

Under light (less than 10 Knots) wind conditions 10° descending on the end of the downwind leg, 25° on base, and full flaps over the threshold as required. In heavier winds 25° or less is good flap setting for landing. Use minimum flap setting possible for cross wind landing.
In gusty winds add 1/2 difference between gust and average wind speed to approach speed.
Touchdown — Just above stalling speed - main wheels first.
Landing Roll — Lower nose wheel gently

In gusty winds add 1/2 difference between gust and average wind speed to approach speed.
Touchdown — Roundout must be done much faster than usual due to low airspeed.
Landing Roll — Hold Nose off as long as possible.
